p: say: According as it is written, De 24:4.
be greatly polluted: If he take such a one to wife again.
lovers: That is, with idols, and with them whom you have put your confidence in.
return again to me: And I will not cast you off, but receive you, according to my mercy.
Arabian in the wilderness: Who dwells in tent and waits for them that pass by to rob them.
latter rain: As God threatened by his law, De 28:24.
harlot's forehead: You would never be ashamed of your acts and repent: and this impudency is common to idolaters, who will not cease, though they are openly convicted.
to me: He shows that the wicked in their miseries will cry to God and use outward prayer as the godly do, but because they do not turn from their evil, they are not heard, Isa 58:3,4.
Israel hath done: Meaning the ten tribes.
her away: And gave her into the hands of the Assyrians.
lightness of her harlotry: The Hebrew word may either signify lightness and wantonness, or noise and brute.

her whole heart: Judah pretended for a time that she returned, as under Josiah and other good kings, but she was never truly touched, or wholly reformed, as appeared when opportunity was offered by any wicked prince.
justified herself more than treacherous Judah: Israel has not declared herself as wicked as Judah, who yet has had more admonitions and examples to call her to repentance.
the north: While the Israelites were now kept in captivity by the Assyrians, to whom he promises mercy, if they will repent.
scattered thy ways to the strangers: There was no way which you did not hunt to seek after the idols, and to go on a pilgrimage.
ark of the covenant of the: This is to be understood of the coming of Christ: for then they will not seek the Lord by ceremonies, and all figures will cease.
the throne of the LORD: Meaning, the Church, where the Lord will be present to the world's end, Mt 28:20.
north to the land that I: Where they are now in captivity.
husband: The Hebrew word signifies a friend or companion, and here may be taken for a husband, as it is used also in Ho 3:1.
A voice was heard upon the: Signifying, that God, whom they had forsaken, would bring their enemies to them, who would lead them captive, and make them to cry and lament.
Behold: This is spoken in the person of Israel to the shame of Judah, who stayed so long to turn to God.
fathers from our youth: For their idolatry God's vengeance has light on them and theirs.

for we have sinned against the: They justify not themselves, or say that they would follow their fathers, but condemn their wicked doings and desire forgiveness for the same, as in Ezr 9:7, Ps 106:6, Isa 64:6.
